name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,327

clue.text: Mystery of hydrogen bond regularly seen in white element

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word before it, here the even ones
something seen in a place sits inside it, so the first pieces go inside the outer ones

blocks.note: W is a standard abbreviation for white
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen
the second and fourth letters of bond
an element is a component or unit

explanation.surface: A chemistry puzzle about a hydrogen bond turning up in some white element.
explanation.walkthrough: W is a recognised abbreviation for white; the hydrogen and bond letters sit between it and the element.
explanation.definitionFit: A whodunit is a detective story, a crime novel or play built around solving a mystery.

clue.text: A new meal is cooked with soldiers' kitchen equipment perhaps

indicators.note: cooking changes the ingredients, so the preceding words are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
RE is the Royal Engineers, a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: A fresh meal cooked in the army's pots and pans.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes all three words, new included, rather than reading new as N.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamelware is metal cookware coated in enamel, such as pans and mugs, an example of kitchen gear.

clue.text: Even the Spanish left a worker in the eastern Mediterranean

indicators.note: the Spanish word for the has left, departing from the word before it

blocks.note: even and level both mean flat or equal
el is Spanish for the
a worker ant

explanation.surface: A level-headed Spaniard leaves a labourer behind in the eastern Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: LEVEL loses its final EL to leave LEV, then ANT is added. 'Left' looks like L but signals the departure.
explanation.definitionFit: The Levant is the historical name for the lands along the eastern shore of the Mediterranean Sea.

clue.text: Most devoted son found in privy

indicators.note: a thing found in another lies inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
a privy is a toilet, also called a water closet

explanation.surface: A doting son discovered in the lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes inside CLOSET. Privy is an old word for a lavatory, and closet survives in water closet.
explanation.definitionFit: Closest describes the most intimate or most attached friend, so it suits a superlative for devoted.

clue.text: Surfing king swallows drug for a joke

indicators.note: whatever swallows something holds it inside, so the drug goes within the other letters

blocks.note: surfing the web means being online
R for rex, Latin for king
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A monarch on a surfboard downs some drug to get a laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: The drug goes inside the combined surfing and king letters, after their first two letters, not at either end.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-liner is a short quip or wisecrack delivered in a single sentence, a kind of joke.

clue.text: Dog ripping side from meat

indicators.note: ripping something from a thing tears it away, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: the on side is one half of a cricket field
mutton is meat from a sheep

explanation.surface: A dog tearing a flank off a joint of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: MUTTON loses ON to leave MUTT. In cricket the on side, or leg side, is one half of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutt is an informal word for a dog, usually a mongrel of mixed breed.

clue.text: Gives lots of directions about party

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the compass letters go around the party

blocks.note: four compass points: east, north, west, south
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Someone hands out plenty of instructions about a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Directions' looks like instructions, but here it means points of the compass.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to give money or property as a lasting gift, or to provide someone with a quality.

clue.text: Key principle used in teaching English

indicators.note: used in says the letters are found inside the following words, spanning them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A core rule applied when teaching English.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across teacHING English.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinge, figuratively, is the central point or principle on which everything else turns or depends.

clue.text: Heather meets head of institute in college for food

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
in places one piece inside the next, here within the college

blocks.note: ling is another name for heather
uni is short for university
first letter of institute

explanation.surface: Heather meets the director of an institute at college to get some dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' reads as a woman's name but is the plant, also called ling.
explanation.definitionFit: Linguini is a type of flat, narrow pasta, and so an example of food.

clue.text: Revolutionary took home cheese

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns round, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: to take home a sum is to make or earn it

explanation.surface: A rebel carried some cheese back to the house.
explanation.walkthrough: Took home means earned, as in take-home pay, so MADE, which reads EDAM backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a mild Dutch cheese, usually sold in a ball with red wax coating.

clue.text: Awful lout in Bosnia mistakenly gets pardon

indicators.note: something awful is in a bad state, so the word after it is jumbled
done mistakenly means put in the wrong order, so the country's name is jumbled too
in places the first jumbled word inside the second

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dreadful hooligan in the Balkans is wrongly let off.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams, each with its own indicator; the jumbled hooligan goes inside the jumbled country.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolution is formal forgiveness or release from guilt, especially of sins, so a pardon.

clue.text: Exaggerates smart apartment with ease oddly

indicators.note: oddly keeps only the letters in odd positions of the word before it

blocks.note: in means fashionable
a flat is an apartment
first and third letters of ease

explanation.surface: Someone talks up a stylish apartment as unusually comfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' means fashionable here, as does IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflate figures or claims is to blow them up beyond the truth, which is to exaggerate.

clue.text: Letter to the Corinthians beginning to describe first Adam?

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet, the one Corinthians used
first letter of describe
1st written as I and ST

explanation.surface: A biblical letter to Corinth starts describing the first man, Adam.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter is not Paul's epistle but a Greek letter, as Corinth was Greek. First is written 1ST, the 1 read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam went without clothes in Eden, so the question mark marks him as an example of someone naked.

clue.text: What may be unpardonable in Disney - lads rioting

indicators.note: rioting lads run wild, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Boys running riot at Disney are behaving unforgivably.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadly sins, or mortal sins, are in Christian teaching the gravest wrongs, those that may not be forgiven.

clue.text: Unfortunately retains a fatty compound

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the word's letters are disordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Sadly, the body holds on to some fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Stearin is a glyceride of stearic acid, the main constituent of many animal fats and used in candles.

clue.text: Where a bird may be on everyone's mind

blocks.note: first meaning: aloft, flying
second meaning: a feeling or idea widely sensed

explanation.walkthrough: A literal location for something flying, and an idiom for a mood or rumour that everyone senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the phrase means up in the sky; idiomatically it describes something sensed or talked about generally.

clue.text: Soldiers secure old US resort

blocks.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
to land a deal is to secure it
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Troops capture an outdated American holiday spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando in Florida is a famous American holiday destination, home to Disney World and other theme parks.

clue.text: Statesman - one supporting the return of King James?

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the name is read backwards

blocks.note: King Lear, Shakespeare's tragic monarch
Sid James, the comic actor of the Carry On films
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone backs the restoration of King James to the throne, a Jacobite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King James' reads as one monarch but is two people: LEAR, and Sid James, a British comedy actor. In a down clue, supporting means I goes underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli was a Victorian statesman who twice served as British Prime Minister.

clue.text: Stop European doctor on ship

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A continental medic on board a ship is told to halt.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban or halt, especially on trade, so it works as a noun for a stop.

clue.text: Admit playfully judge has fallen for Victor

indicators.note: one thing falling and being exchanged for another means a letter is swapped out

blocks.note: said playfully means said in jest
J is the abbreviation for judge
Victor is V in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone jokingly admits the judge has fallen for a man named Victor.
explanation.walkthrough: IN JEST has its J replaced by V.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest someone is to install them formally in office or rank, which is to admit them to it.

clue.text: Exposed North American shop-lifting!

indicators.note: in a down answer lifting raises the word, so it is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: NA is the abbreviation for North American
a deli is a delicatessen shop

explanation.surface: An American caught red-handed shoplifting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shop-lifting' looks like the crime, but it splits into the shop and its lifting.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail a lie or a culprit is to expose or catch them out, so nailed means exposed.

clue.text: Righteous person’s spoken wearing veil

indicators.note: the spoken word is wearing the veil, which therefore wraps round it

blocks.note: oral means spoken
a mist is a veil that hides things

explanation.surface: A pious person speaks from behind a veil.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for is, joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A moralist is someone who preaches or upholds strict morals, a self-consciously righteous person.

clue.text: Crew aspires to cover up hand tool

indicators.note: the words cover the answer, so it sits inside them
in a down answer up means reading from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: the letters at the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A team hopes to hide the tools.
explanation.walkthrough: It is hidden backwards in creW ASPIRes.
explanation.definitionFit: A ripsaw is a handsaw with coarse teeth for cutting wood along the grain, a hand tool.

clue.text: Decide a map needs re-plotting for adjutant

indicators.note: plotting something afresh puts its parts in new places

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An officer's assistant must redraw the route on the map.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide-de-camp is a military officer acting as personal assistant to a senior officer, as an adjutant does.

clue.text: Harmful pest we eradicated

indicators.note: eradicated means wiped out, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: a weevil is a beetle that is a crop pest
taken as written

explanation.surface: We wiped out a damaging pest.
explanation.walkthrough: WEEVIL with WE removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Evil means wicked or causing great harm, so it is an adjective for something harmful.

clue.text: Quiet expression of scepticism about leader

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the expression is read backwards

blocks.note: sh is a call for quiet
ha is a scoffing exclamation

explanation.surface: A muted scoff about the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shah was the title of the monarch of Iran, a ruler or head of state.

clue.text: Justifying virgin Queen's time imprisoned by evil emperor

indicators.note: whatever is imprisoned is locked inside, so these letters go within the emperor

blocks.note: Ming the Merciless, villainous emperor of the Flash Gordon stories
Elizabeth I, the Virgin Queen, is ER I
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Elizabeth I's era held captive by a wicked emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the royal cipher for Elizabeth Regina, so the Virgin Queen, Elizabeth the First, is ER I.
explanation.definitionFit: Meriting something is deserving it, which justifies it, so the participles match in sense and form.

clue.text: Cancel circular without a right

indicators.note: without means lacking, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: annular means ring-shaped, circular
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Withdraw a leaflet that omits a legal entitlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circular' looks like a leaflet but is the adjective, ANNULAR, which loses A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul is to declare void or invalid, as with a marriage or contract, which is to cancel it.
